llm.summary: The skill's stated purpose (local UDP agent messaging) matches what its instructions ask you to install and run, but it directs you to install unreviewed code from a third‑party GitHub repo and open a network socket — a coherent but potentially risky combination that warrants caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (UDP LAN messaging) aligns with the declared requirements and runtime instructions: node is required because the plugin is a TypeScript/Node module, and the tools described (discover, send, receive, approve, etc.) are exactly what a UDP messenger would provide.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md stays within the stated purpose: it describes discovery, sending, receiving, trust model, and configuration and explicitly instructs the agent to prompt the user before trusting peers or sharing sensitive data. It also instructs periodic checks during long tasks (which is reasonable for message handling) but gives the agent discretion to poll during work — that behavior increases the timeframe in which incoming network messages might affect an agent's activity and should be considered.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no built-in install spec in the registry, but the SKILL.md tells users to run `openclaw plugins install https://github.com/turfptax/openclaw-udp-messenger.git` (and includes metadata referencing a localPath). This causes the platform to fetch and run third‑party plugin code from a personal GitHub repo rather than a reviewed package or trusted release. Fetching and installing arbitrary repository code is a moderate-to-high risk because it executes external code that can open sockets, read files, or exfiltrate data; the SKILL.md does not provide a pinned release hash or attest to code review.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials and only needs a network port and optional config (port, trustMode, maxExchanges). The lack of secret or unrelated credential requests is appropriate for a local LAN messaging tool.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (not force-included) and model invocation is allowed (the platform default). The plugin registers tools and opens a UDP socket when installed — that is expected for this plugin, but combined with autonomous invocation it widens the blast radius if the plugin is malicious or misconfigured. The SKILL.md's trust rules mitigate some risk but cannot enforce behavior if the plugin itself is malicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says (local UDP messaging) but installation requires pulling and running third‑party code from a personal GitHub repository. Before installing: (1) review the plugin repository code (or ask the author for a signed/released package); (2) prefer a pinned release tag/commit hash rather than installing from 'main'; (3) install only on a non-sensitive machine or inside an isolated environment if you want to experiment; (4) configure trustMode to 'always-confirm' and set a low maxExchanges; (5) do not enable the plugin on networks where sensitive data or credentials could be exposed; (6) consider asking for the plugin author's identity/reputation or for the plugin to be published via a trusted registry. Because the plugin will open a network socket and can send/receive arbitrary messages, treat it as potentially capable of exfiltration unless you audit the code.
